info.title: Forge API
info.description: F04 accepted contract. Product routes are not implemented by F03. OIDC/ownership, persistence and Temporal must be integrated before enabling mutations. Rejected/deferred: arbitrary tools, writable/network permissions, CPU/memory requests, deployment policy and desired state.

post.description: No request body. Repeated requests return 202 and one logical cancel command. Serialize cancel after start delivery. Completion may win the race; accepted cancellation does not guarantee canceled execution.

post.summary: Accept controlled rerun of own terminal run
post.description: No request body. Authenticate/authorize, then check owner/key/fingerprint before evaluating a new rerun. A matching accepted retry returns its existing run even during a Temporal outage. For a new rerun, require currently confirmed terminal status; unavailable Temporal returns 503. Copy original version/question/source selection into a new run and set rerun_of. A new run may regenerate results and is not replay. Idempotency scope is shared with createRun; fingerprint includes operation and parent run.

BearerAuth.description: Real OIDC API access token from configured Keycloak issuer. Validate issuer/audience/signature/expiry and configured role claim; ownership is (iss,sub). No fake identity or auth placeholder.

ID.description: Server-issued lowercase UUID v4. A Forge run ID is not a Temporal execution Run ID.

DocumentID.description: Corpus document identifier, never a path or URL.

Cursor.description: Opaque server-issued cursor bound to caller, collection and filters. Never a substitute for authorization.

IdempotencyKey.description: Scoped to validated issuer/subject for all run submissions, including reruns. Retained for the lifetime of the run record.

WorkloadName.description: Unique within an owner; case-sensitive lowercase slug.

document_ids.description: Requested source scope. Registration requires platform approval of snapshot/document availability; a valid schema alone grants no access.

tools.description: Exactly these read-only tools. Worker selects fixed stages; model cannot add tools.

model_id.description: Requested testing model. No paid/model/provider fallback; routing policy is operator-owned.

document_ids.description: Required explicit subset of the immutable version source scope.

oneOf.description: Only report not_started when the dispatcher can establish that no start has occurred. Pending acknowledgement alone is not proof.

ExecutionStatus.description: Temporal is authoritative. Unavailable state is unknown; a cached last-known state cannot be reported as current. A cached last-known state and its observation timestamp must be present together; the timestamp is the cache observation, not the failed lookup time.

Run.description: Submission/cancellation are PostgreSQL handoff states, not execution outcomes. Pending acknowledgement permits a Temporal observation after an ambiguous start. Delivered cancellation requires dispatched submission; dispatched submission cannot claim not_started.
